source.table: DSDT, captured from the emulated profile (vendor UEFI 2.158.15)
source.how: tests/fixtures/nvram_census.c writes the tables the firmware publishes into the run directory

FIF.meaning: Revision 0, fine-grained control, step size 1, low-speed notification 1

FPS.note: present but unused for state mapping: fine-grained control wins

interface.level_zero_meaning: 975 rpm, the slowest the firmware drives the fans; there is no automatic level in this interface

smc.note: one _FSL on either fan writes all four commands with the same rpm

FST_returns: control (the last level written, from AML state)
speed in rpm (from the SMC reply)

write_path_measured.unit: one ACUM027 unit, Secure Boot off, module built with the unit's own kbuild
write_path_measured.level_scale_is_a_floor: the _FSL scale maps level 0..100 to 975 + 3375*level/100 rpm, i.e. 975 to 4350 rpm. That is a floor, not a fan setting: level 100 asks for 4350 rpm and the EC is free to run above it. Two different levels are therefore often the same setting to the EC, which is why an A/B on the level measured nothing
write_path_measured.transport_takes_rpm: the write commands 0x06000790..0x06000793 carry the rpm itself as two little-endian bytes, so a floor above the _FSL scale can be asked for directly: rpm_floor=13500 was written and the service then reported 8820/12420 rpm. The quiet third-party project on the same hardware reports the fans reaching 9000/13500 rpm, which is consistent
write_path_measured.heard: with the 13500 floor the machine is audibly louder than the other units on the same desk — the corroboration the tachometer cannot give, since both come from the same service

thermal_observation.what: the same 8-worker CPU load was run for the same duration under three settings and the hottest thermal zone sampled once a second
thermal_observation.reading: the high floor held the machine 6 C cooler under the same load
thermal_observation.not_a_benchmark: one run per arm, no repetition, no control for ambient or for the EC's own policy; this is an observation, not a controlled performance benchmark. The cooling-rate arms of the same script produced no measurement because the machine never rose above the cool-to target in two of the three arms
thermal_observation.not_a_benchmark_precedent: the third-party project states the same limit about its own thermal runs, and this record follows it

write_path_measured.does_not_revert: nothing in this interface releases the EC's clamps: unloading the module and writing pwm1_enable=2 both leave the last floor in place. A reboot is the only restore, which is why the module refuses to write without allow_pin=1
write_path_measured.read_warmup: a status read answers 0 on the first call after a gap and the rpm on the second; both status ids behave the same way

cross_version.what_was_compared: the fan AML in two DSDTs we hold: the capsule's (vendor UEFI 2.158.15, which reports BIOS 5.36_0ACUM028) and a unit's own (BIOS 5.36_0ACUM027)

acum027_units.dsdt: no Device (FAN0), no _FSL, no _FST, no WFCF, and none of the four write literals 0x06000790..0x06000793 (grep count 0)
acum027_units.service: the SMC service is present anyway: measured on one ACUM027 unit, reads answered 4320 rpm, tracked writes moved the fans, and a 13500 rpm floor produced 8820/12420 rpm and an audible increase

acum028_capsule.dsdt: Device (FAN0) present with _FSL/_FST/WFCF and the four write literals
acum028_capsule.service: not measured: no ACUM028 unit was available; the monitor's model of the service is not evidence about firmware

dsdt_detail.call: _FSL -> WFCF -> WRB with XX0 = 0xC400008D and XX1 = 0x8003 (dsdt.dsl:16111-16112, 16149-16150)
dsdt_detail.write: WFCF writes 0x06000790..0x06000793 with the rpm low byte then high byte, both fans (dsdt.dsl:16120-16133)
dsdt_detail.scale: RPM = FMIN + ((FMAX - FMIN) * level) / 0x64 with FMIN = 0x3CF (975) and FMAX = 0x10FE (4350) (dsdt.dsl:16062-16063)
dsdt_detail.consequence: the function id, endpoint, command ids and level scale this module uses are the newest firmware's own AML constants, not values inferred from behaviour. What is still unproven on ACUM028 is the service that answers behind the call

cross_version.reading: the constants this model uses come from the *newer* firmware's DSDT and work on the older units whose ACPI does not publish a fan device at all, because the module talks to the service directly and needs no ACPI. New-to-old is measured; old-to-new and anything later is inference

confidence.acum027_units: high - measured end to end on one unit, and all three live units run this build
confidence.acum028: high by construction, unproven in execution - the newest firmware's DSDT calls this exact function id and endpoint and writes these exact commands with this exact scale, so the interface is the firmware's own; no ACUM028 unit has been available to confirm that the service answers
confidence.later_firmware: inference, not evidence: the function id, endpoint, GUID, status ids and command base are compiled in, so a firmware that moves any of them breaks it. The failure mode is a refused read (the module fails closed) rather than a wrong write

cross_version.what_would_raise_it: run tools/fan_verify.sh read-only on an ACUM028 unit and compare against the ACUM027 baseline in docs/fan-verify-on-a-unit.md. The remaining question is not whether the interface exists - the firmware documents it - but whether the EC behind it answers on that build

third_image_asus.what: the third firmware the emulator supports, version 4.1.0, whose banner reads 0ACUM10 -- a different lineage from 0ACUM027/0ACUM028 and the ASUS Ascent image

firmware_calls_the_fan_service_itself.meaning: the image's own code drives the fan/EC endpoint during boot, before any OS runs, so the interface is live in that firmware even though its DSDT does not describe it

third_image_asus.what_it_proves_and_what_it_does_not: It proves the transport path exists and is used by that firmware. It does not prove any value was written to the fans, and it says nothing about an ACPI floor: 4.1.0's DSDT carries no FAN0, no _FSL/_FST and no WFCF, exactly like 0ACUM027, so a _FSL-based control has no object to write on this firmware and only the SMC path can be used.
